sense: of a country: its trade, industry and money

evidence: M-O s.v. depression: recession: jacent commercia, we are in a recession
terms.comment: Classically trade and dealings (per commercia et negōtiātōrēs, Tac. Agr. 24); Morgan–Owens extends the plural to a country’s economy. Latin has no classical word for the economy as a whole (see economic).

terms.gloss: credit, the trust that lending rests on
evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 19: fidem concidisse, credit had collapsed
Caes. BC 3.1.2: cum fidēs tōtā Ītaliā esset angustior
terms.comment: The Romans spoke of an economy in trouble through its credit: fidēs collapsed (concidit) or tightened (angustior).

phrases.latin: haec fidēs atque haec ratiō pecūniārum, quae Rōmae, quae in forō versātur, implicāta est cum illīs pecūniīs Asiāticīs et cohaeret
phrases.english: this credit, this whole system of money that operates at Rome and in the Forum, is bound up with that money in Asia and hangs together with it

phrases.latin: cum fidēs tōtā Ītaliā esset angustior neque crēditae pecūniae solverentur
phrases.english: since credit was tighter all over Italy and loans were not being repaid

sources: Lewis & Short: commercium · Lewis & Short: fides
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. economy; depression: recession.
